what-do-bed-bugs-look-like-on-a-bed-a-me.title: What Do Bed Bugs Look Like on a Bed? A Mesa Homeowner's Inspection Guide
what-do-bed-bugs-look-like-on-a-bed-a-me.content:
Adult bed bugs look like flat, reddish-brown, oval insects about the size of an apple seed (roughly 4–5 mm), and on a bed you will usually spot them, or the evidence they leave, along the mattress seams, piping, tags and headboard. If you live in Mesa and you are checking your own bed right now, look for live bugs, tiny pale eggs, translucent shed skins and small dark specks that smear rust-colored when wiped. Everything below is what we look for when we walk into a Mesa bedroom, and it is the same checklist you can run in about ten minutes with a flashlight. If you confirm a problem, our team handles bed bug treatment in Mesa from inspection through follow-up.

What Do Bed Bugs Look Like on a Bed?

Bed bugs on a bed look like small, flat, rust-brown ovals that hide in folds and seams rather than sitting out on the sheet. Fed bugs are swollen, darker and more elongated. Young bugs are pale, straw-colored and can be as small as a pinhead. Most people never see a bug in daylight because they tuck into tight cracks, so the signs around the bug are often what you notice first.

Across homes from Dobson Ranch to Eastmark, we see the same pattern. The bugs cluster within a few feet of where someone sleeps, and the first clue is almost never a crawling bug. It is a cluster of dark specks on the mattress piping, a faint blood spot on a pillowcase, or a bite pattern that shows up every morning.

How Big Is a Bed Bug at Each Life Stage?

A bed bug goes through five nymph stages before adulthood, and each stage has to feed on blood before it molts. That is why size varies so much, and why a bed can hold bugs that look like completely different insects. The table below is how we describe each stage to Mesa homeowners during an inspection.

StageApproximate sizeWhat it looks like
EggAbout 1 mmPearly white, rice-shaped, glued into seams and crevices
Young nymph1.5–2 mmTranslucent, straw-colored, nearly invisible until fed
Older nymph3–4.5 mmTan to light brown, turns reddish after feeding
Unfed adult4–5 mmFlat, oval, mahogany brown, like an apple seed
Fed adult5–7 mmSwollen, longer, dark red to purplish-brown

Where Do I Look First When I Check My Bed for Bed Bugs?

Start at the mattress seams and work outward, because bed bugs hide closest to the person they feed on. Pull the sheets off, turn on a bright flashlight and work in this order:

  1. Mattress piping and seams, especially the head-end corners, where bugs and dark specks collect.
  2. The tag and the underside of the mattress, including the fabric that covers the box spring.
  3. Headboard joints and bed-frame screw holes, which make perfect tight hiding spots.
  4. Nightstand drawers and the gap between the nightstand and the wall.
  5. Baseboards, outlet covers and the edge of the carpet within a few feet of the bed.

A credit card run gently along the seam is a good trick. It pulls out eggs and shed skins that a flashlight alone misses.

What Do Bed Bug Signs Look Like Besides the Bugs Themselves?

The evidence is often easier to find than the insect. These are the signs we point to most often, and finding two or more of them together is a strong indicator of an active infestation:

  • Dark fecal spots. Tiny black or rust-colored dots, about the size of a pen tip, that bleed into the fabric when dampened.
  • Blood smears. Small reddish stains on sheets or pillowcases where a fed bug was crushed.
  • Shed skins. Hollow, translucent, tan shells left behind each time a nymph molts.
  • Eggs and egg shells. Clusters of tiny white specks stuck in seams.
  • A sweet, musty odor. In heavier infestations, some people notice it when they open a closet or pull back bedding.

What Do Bed Bug Bites Look Like?

Bed bug bites are small, red, itchy welts that often show up in lines or clusters on skin exposed while sleeping, such as the arms, neck, face and shoulders. Reactions vary a lot, and some people show no reaction at all. Because mosquito, flea and spider bites can look nearly identical, a bite pattern alone can never confirm bed bugs. You need to find the bug or its signs.

That matters in Mesa, where people sometimes blame bites on mosquitoes after a monsoon. If the bites appear only after sleeping, and never while you are outside in the evening, check the bed before you buy more repellent. If mosquitoes really are the issue, our mosquito control service in Mesa and this guide to stopping mosquitoes in the 85208 area cover that side.

How Do Bed Bugs Get Into Mesa Homes?

Bed bugs are hitchhikers, not a sign of a dirty home. They travel in luggage, backpacks, used furniture and clothing, then settle in wherever people sleep. Mesa has more of that traffic than most people realize, which is why we treat it as a local risk instead of a rare one.

  • Travel and visitors. Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport, spring training crowds around Sloan Park and winter visitors all bring luggage through neighborhoods across 85201–85210.
  • Multi-unit housing. Apartments and rentals near downtown Mesa, Mesa Community College and the Superstition Springs area share walls, which lets bugs move between units.
  • Used furniture. Secondhand couches, mattresses and headboards are a classic way to bring a hidden population home.
  • College and shared living. Students and roommates moving in and out move bedding and boxes with them.

Heat does not protect a Mesa home. Bed bugs live indoors at a steady temperature, so a 110°F July does not slow them down the way it slows outdoor pests. If you want the treatment side of the story, our Mesa neighborhood guide to bed bug treatment around Red Mountain walks through what happens after a confirmed find.

Is It Bed Bugs or Something Else?

Several common Arizona household insects get mistaken for bed bugs. Telling them apart saves you from treating the wrong problem. Here is how we sort them out:

Look-alikeHow it differs from a bed bug
Carpet beetle larvaeFuzzy and bristly, often found near wool and closets, and they do not bite
Cockroach nymphsFaster, with longer legs and antennae, and they run when the light comes on
FleasJump, are much smaller, and bites concentrate on ankles and lower legs
Spider beetlesRound and shiny with long legs, usually near stored food
TicksEight legs instead of six, and usually linked to pets

If what you found runs fast and hides behind appliances, see our guide to getting rid of cockroaches in Mesa. If it is a tiny web builder hiding in corners, our Mesa spider guide is a better fit.

What Should I Do If I Find Bed Bugs?

Stay calm, contain the problem and get a professional inspection. Bed bugs spread fastest when people panic and start moving things around. We suggest the following:

  1. Wash and dry bedding on high heat, then bag it until treatment is finished.
  2. Vacuum seams, baseboards and the bed frame, then empty the vacuum outside into a sealed bag.
  3. Do not move items into other rooms or bring in sprays from the store. Over-the-counter products often scatter bugs to new rooms.
  4. Do not toss your mattress until we have inspected. Moving it uncovered can spread bugs through the hallway and into other rooms.
  5. Call us so a technician can confirm the species, find every harborage and build a plan for your home.

We are locally owned and Apache Junction based, have served Arizona families since 2013, and are an AZ ROC licensed team. You can call us in Mesa at (480) 422-8388 or request service online. If a neighbor, apartment or relative is also dealing with bed bugs, tell us. It changes how we plan the job.

Yes, and we see the same signs throughout the East Valley. We service Gilbert, Chandler, Tempe, Queen Creek, Apache Junction and Gold Canyon, and the inspection steps above apply to all of them. Our neighbors in Gilbert can read our Gilbert 85295 bed bug guide and see our bed bug treatment in Gilbert page, and Queen Creek residents can check the Cortina bed bug guide. Frequently Asked Questions About What Bed Bugs Look Like

What do bed bugs look like to the naked eye?

Adult bed bugs are flat, oval and reddish-brown, about the size of an apple seed, and visible without a magnifier. Young bugs are much smaller and pale, so a flashlight and a close look at seams help.

Can you see bed bugs during the day?

Usually not. Bed bugs hide in seams and cracks during the day and come out mostly at night to feed, so finding dark specks, shed skins or eggs is often easier than spotting a live bug.

What do bed bug eggs look like?

Bed bug eggs are about 1 mm long, pearly white and shaped like a tiny grain of rice. They are usually stuck in clusters along mattress seams, headboard joints and other tight crevices.

What do bed bugs look like after they feed?

After feeding, a bed bug becomes swollen, longer and noticeably darker, often dark red to purplish-brown. A recently fed bug also moves more slowly than a hungry one.

Do bed bugs only live in beds?

No. Beds are the most common spot, but bugs also hide in couches, recliners, baseboards, outlet covers and behind picture frames, especially in heavier infestations.

Are bed bugs a sign that my Mesa home is dirty?

No. Bed bugs travel on luggage, clothing and secondhand furniture, and they show up in clean homes, hotels and apartments alike. Cleanliness does not cause them.

how-to-get-rid-of-fruit-mosquitoes-a-mes.title: How to Get Rid of Fruit Mosquitoes: A Mesa Homeowner's Guide to Fruit Flies and Gnats
how-to-get-rid-of-fruit-mosquitoes-a-mes.content:
The tiny "mosquitoes" hovering over your fruit bowl are almost never mosquitoes. They are fruit flies, and you get rid of them by removing whatever they breed in (ripe fruit, a wet drain, a damp trash can), then trapping the adults that are left. If you live in Mesa and the cloud is thick around the kitchen, start with the checklist below, and if the problem is actually biting mosquitoes outside, our team handles mosquito control in Mesa. You can also call us at (480) 422-8388.

How Do You Get Rid of Fruit Mosquitoes?

You get rid of fruit "mosquitoes" in three steps: find and remove the breeding material, clean the drains and bins where eggs hide, and trap the adults until the last ones disappear. Traps alone never finish the job, because a single overlooked banana or slow drain keeps producing a new generation every week or so.

Here is the order we recommend to Mesa homeowners, from Dobson Ranch to Eastmark:

  1. Clear the food source. Throw out overripe fruit, refrigerate produce, and check the pantry for a forgotten potato, onion or bottle of juice.
  2. Empty and wash the trash and recycling. Sticky residue in the bottom of a bin is a perfect nursery.
  3. Clean the drains. Scrub the inside of kitchen and bathroom drains with a stiff brush, because the film on the pipe wall is what drain flies feed on.
  4. Set a simple trap. A small jar with a little apple cider vinegar, a drop of dish soap and a paper funnel catches adults overnight.
  5. Repeat for a week. Eggs you missed will hatch, so keep traps out and sources clean for at least seven to ten days.

Are Fruit Mosquitoes Really Mosquitoes?

No. People search "fruit mosquitoes" for the small flying insects that swarm ripe fruit, but they are usually fruit flies (Drosophila), and sometimes fungus gnats or drain flies. True mosquitoes bite, need standing water to breed, and are mostly a patio and yard problem, not a kitchen one.

The confusion is understandable. All of these insects are small, dark and annoying, and they tend to show up together in summer. The quickest way to tell them apart is to look at where they gather and how they fly.

Fruit Fly vs. Drain Fly vs. Fungus Gnat vs. Mosquito

InsectWhat it looks likeWhere you find itWhat it breeds inBites?
Fruit flyTan to brown, red eyes, about the size of a pinheadFruit bowl, trash can, recycling, sinkRipe or rotting produce, sticky residueNo
Drain flyFuzzy, moth-like, grey wings held like a tentBathroom and kitchen drains, shower wallsSlime film inside slow drainsNo
Fungus gnatSlim, dark, long legs, weak flyerHouseplants, near windowsConstantly wet potting soilNo
MosquitoLong legs, slender body, long mouthpartsPatio, yard, shaded walls, bedrooms at nightStanding water that sits for daysYes

If the insects are in the kitchen and never bite, treat it as a sanitation problem. If you are getting bitten, read our Mesa guide to stopping mosquitoes instead.

Why Do Fruit Flies Show Up So Fast in Mesa Homes?

Mesa's heat speeds up everything a fruit fly needs. Produce ripens faster on the counter, trash warms up quickly in the garage, and a female can lay hundreds of eggs that hatch within a day or two. One forgotten peach can turn into a swarm in days.

Across the 85201 through 85210 ZIP codes, we see the same handful of triggers, and several are specific to the valley:

  • Backyard citrus and fruit trees. Fallen oranges, lemons and grapefruit that bake on the ground ferment quickly and draw flies right to your back door.
  • Garage trash and recycling bins. Bins that sit in the heat develop a sour film that flies love, and the smell travels through the garage door.
  • Monsoon humidity. When the humidity jumps in July through September, damp sink traps, wet sponges and overwatered houseplants hold moisture longer.
  • Disposal and dishwasher gunk. Food residue under the disposal flange is one of the most common hidden breeding spots we find.
  • Wine, beer and juice bottles. A recycling bin of unrinsed bottles is an open invitation, especially near the Fiesta District and other busy households.

What Is the Fastest Way to Kill Fruit Flies in the House?

The fastest safe method is a vinegar trap plus removing the breeding source the same day. The trap kills the adults you can see within hours, while cleaning the source stops the next wave. A fly swatter or spray only kills what is flying right now.

How Do You Make a Fruit Fly Trap?

Pour about an inch of apple cider vinegar into a jar, add a drop of dish soap so the flies sink instead of landing on the surface, and cover the top with plastic wrap poked with small holes, or a rolled paper cone. Set one near the fruit bowl and another near the kitchen sink.

Does Bleach or Boiling Water Clear Drain Flies?

Bleach and boiling water rarely solve it because they run straight past the film on the pipe wall. A stiff brush, a bit of baking soda and hot tap water, or an enzyme drain cleaner from the store, reaches the slime where the larvae live. Do this nightly for a week.

A quick test helps you confirm a drain is the source: tape a piece of clear plastic wrap over the drain opening overnight. If small flies are stuck to the underside in the morning, you have found the nursery.

How Long Do Fruit Flies Take to Go Away?

Once the breeding source is gone, most infestations fade in one to two weeks. The life cycle in warm Arizona kitchens can be as short as a week from egg to adult, so eggs and larvae you missed keep hatching for several days. If flies are still there after two weeks, there is a source you have not found.

Hidden Breeding Spots People Miss

  • The rubber gasket inside the dishwasher door
  • Under the refrigerator drip tray
  • The bottom of the garbage disposal and its rubber splash guard
  • Mop heads and dish rags that stay damp
  • Pet food dishes and water bowls left out overnight
  • Overflow drains in bathroom sinks and floor drains in the garage or laundry room
  • Compost buckets and worm bins kept indoors

When Is It Not Fruit Flies but Real Mosquitoes?

If you are getting bitten, especially around ankles, in the evening or overnight, you are dealing with mosquitoes, not fruit flies. Mosquitoes breed in standing water that sits for more than a few days, and in Mesa that usually means a neglected pool, a clogged gutter, a plant saucer or an irrigation low spot.

In the monsoon months we get the most calls about this. After a storm, water collects in unexpected places, and it only takes a bottle cap of water to get a start. Our neighbors in Gilbert and Chandler deal with the same thing, and we cover the pattern in our Morrison Ranch monsoon guide and the Cooper Commons version.

Where Do Mosquitoes Breed Around a Mesa Yard?

  • Pool covers that collect rainwater
  • Plant saucers and decorative pots
  • Clogged rain gutters and downspout extenders
  • Birdbaths and pet bowls that are not refreshed
  • Low spots where irrigation water pools
  • Drip-line leaks and overflowing evaporative cooler pans

Mosquitoes hide in shaded, humid spots during the day, such as dense shrubs, patio corners and under eaves. Our technicians check those areas first when they visit a property near Red Mountain or Val Vista.

What Can a Pest Control Company Do About Fruit Flies?

A pro inspection finds the source you cannot see, which is the hard part. We look in drains, under appliances, in garage bins and around outdoor fruit trees, and we tell you exactly what is feeding the flies. Sanitation does most of the work, and we are straightforward about that.

What we do not do is pretend a spray fixes a dirty drain. If the flies are in the kitchen, we will show you the source, tell you what to clean, and follow up if it is part of a bigger pest issue. If the real trouble is biting mosquitoes outside or another pest entirely, we handle that too. Our Mesa pest control services cover the full list, and you can request service online any time.

Is It Bed Bugs, Not Flies?

Occasionally. If you are finding bites and no flying insects, the cause may be something else entirely. Our guide on what bed bugs look like on a bed walks through the signs, and our Mesa bed bug treatment page explains what happens next. Roaches can also show up around kitchen drains, which we cover in our Lehi district roach guide.

A Seasonal Checklist for Mesa Kitchens

SeasonWhat to watch forWhat to do
Spring (March to May)Citrus and fruit-tree drop, warming garagesPick up fallen fruit weekly and wash bins monthly
Early summer (June)Heat speeds ripening and trash odorRefrigerate produce and take trash out more often
Monsoon (July to September)Humidity, damp drains, standing water after stormsScrub drains, dump standing water, check plant saucers
Fall (October to November)Holiday produce, cider and bottlesRinse recycling and do not leave fruit out overnight
Winter (December to February)Fewer problems, indoor plants stay wetLet houseplant soil dry between watering

The same flying-insect questions come up across the East Valley, and we have local write-ups for South Tempe and Sossaman Farms in Queen Creek. Frequently Asked Questions

How do you get rid of fruit mosquitoes fast?

Remove overripe fruit, wash trash and recycling bins, scrub the drains, and set a vinegar-and-dish-soap trap. The trap catches adults within hours, and cleaning the source keeps new ones from hatching.

Why do I have tiny mosquito-like bugs in my kitchen?

They are most likely fruit flies, drain flies or fungus gnats. They are attracted to ripe produce, slime in drains and wet potting soil, and they do not bite.

Do fruit flies come from nowhere?

No. Adults arrive on produce from the store or drift in from outside, and eggs on fruit skin hatch quickly in warm kitchens. A small number can become a swarm within days.

Will apple cider vinegar really work on fruit flies?

Yes for catching adults. Fermenting vinegar attracts them, and dish soap breaks the surface tension so they cannot escape. It will not stop breeding, so pair it with cleaning.

When should I call a pest control company?

Call if the flies persist after two weeks of cleaning, if you cannot find the source, or if you are being bitten. Mesa homeowners can reach us at (480) 422-8388.

Are fruit flies dangerous?

They do not bite, but they can carry bacteria from drains and garbage onto food. That is one more reason to deal with the source quickly.

If the flies persist after you clean up, our pest control in Mesa team can inspect for the breeding source.

how-to-get-rid-of-fruit-mosquitoes-a-tuc.title: Drain Flies in Tucson Homes: How to Get Rid of Them for Good
how-to-get-rid-of-fruit-mosquitoes-a-tuc.content:
The tiny gray, moth-shaped flies hanging around your Tucson bathroom or kitchen sink are drain flies, and you get rid of them by cleaning the slime film inside the drain where they breed, not by spraying the flies you can see. Most homes clear in one to two weeks once the film is gone. If the flies keep coming back after that, call us at (520) 284-9930 and our technicians will inspect for the source.

What Are Drain Flies, and Why Are They in My Tucson Home?

Drain flies (also called moth flies or sewer flies) are small, fuzzy, gray-brown insects about 1/8 inch long, with wings held like a tent over the body. They do not bite and they do not carry disease the way a mosquito can, but they are a sure sign that organic gunk is building up somewhere wet. Adults flutter rather than fly, and they usually rest on the wall right next to the drain they came from.

Each female lays dozens of eggs in the film of slime, hair, soap and food residue that coats the inside of a drain or trap. The larvae feed on that film. In warm indoor air the whole cycle can finish in about a week to ten days, which is why a couple of flies in the bathroom can turn into a cloud in a long weekend.

How Do I Know It Is a Drain Fly and Not a Fruit Fly or Gnat?

InsectWhat it looks likeWhere you find itHow it moves
Drain flyFuzzy gray, moth-like wingsBathroom walls, tubs, sinks, floor drainsShort, clumsy flutters
Fruit flyTan body, red eyesFruit bowl, trash, recyclingHovers over food
Fungus gnatSlim, dark, long legsWindows, houseplantsWeak, erratic flight
MosquitoLong legs, needle mouthPatios, bedrooms at nightStraight flight, bites

How Can I Find Which Drain the Flies Are Coming From?

Do the tape test: cover the suspect drain overnight with a piece of clear tape or plastic wrap, then check it in the morning. Flies stuck to the underside mean that drain is a breeding site. Test every drain in the area, because the one you notice is often not the one that is producing them.

  1. Dry the area around the drain so the tape sticks.
  2. Tape clear packing tape across the opening, leaving a small gap for air.
  3. Check it the next morning for small gray flies stuck to the sticky side.
  4. Repeat on bathroom sinks, tub drains, shower drains, the laundry standpipe, the kitchen sink and any floor drain in the garage.

Which Drains Do We See Most Often in Tucson?

  • Guest bathrooms and casita baths. A tub or sink that is used a few times a month never gets flushed, and the film dries into a perfect larval bed.
  • Garage and laundry floor drains. Traps dry out in Tucson heat, then get wet again after a monsoon storm.
  • Kitchen sink overflow holes. The slot behind the faucet collects food film that never sees a brush.
  • Older homes near Sam Hughes, Armory Park and the 85705 and 85719 neighborhoods. Older cast iron lines build more rough film than newer plastic pipe.
  • Rarely used showers in snowbird homes. A home that sits closed for months is a common call for us in Oro Valley and Green Valley.

How Do You Get Rid of Drain Flies for Good?

Scrub the pipe wall with a stiff brush, then treat the drain with an enzyme or bio-based drain cleaner that digests the film. Repeat nightly for a week. Killing adults without removing the film only gives you a short break, because the next batch is already growing in the slime.

What Is the Step-by-Step Drain Cleaning Routine?

  1. Remove the stopper or strainer and pull out hair and debris by hand.
  2. Scrub the inside of the drain opening and the overflow slot with a long, stiff bottle brush.
  3. Pour in an enzyme drain cleaner as directed on the label, and let it sit overnight.
  4. Flush with hot tap water in the morning.
  5. Repeat every night for 7 days, and run water in unused drains weekly after that.

Does Bleach, Boiling Water or Vinegar Work on Drain Flies?

Mostly no. Bleach and hot water run straight down the pipe and skip the sticky film clinging to the walls. They may kill a few larvae, but the film stays. A brush plus an enzyme cleaner is the combination that has worked best in the homes we visit.

Why Do Drain Flies Get Worse During Tucson's Monsoon?

Monsoon humidity (roughly July through September) keeps drain film damp and lets eggs survive in traps and floor drains that normally dry out. Storms can also push moisture and organic debris into outdoor drains, so adults find their way into garages and then into the house.

SeasonWhat happens in TucsonWhat to do
SpringWarm up speeds breeding in lightly used drainsRun water in guest bath and casita drains weekly
Early summerHeat dries traps in garage and laundry drainsPour a cup of water into floor drains monthly
MonsoonHumidity and storm moisture revive breedingBrush and treat drains; check for damp spots near the house
FallLingering warmth, reopened snowbird homesFlush every drain before and after seasonal stays
WinterSlower breeding indoorsKeep up weekly flushing

When Should I Call a Pest Control Company About Drain Flies?

Call us if you have cleaned every drain for two weeks and the flies are still there, if they appear in several rooms at once, or if you cannot find the source. Our technicians inspect the visible drains, the areas around them and the garage and yard, and we work out which insect it is before we treat. We do not offer plumbing work, so if the inspection points to a damaged line, we will tell you that plainly.

A drain fly problem can also be a clue about other pests. Roaches love the same damp spots, so we also check entry points for roach elimination in Tucson, and across the wider Tucson pest and termite services we offer. Our guide to sewer roaches in Tucson explains how drains and roaches travel together, and the roach control guide for central Tucson covers the kitchen side.

Could It Be Spiders, Bed Bugs or Mosquitoes Instead?

If you see lots of webbing near the flies, spiders may be feeding on them; our post on spider control near the University of Arizona explains what we do about that. If something is biting you at night, read the Tucson bed bug guide. Drain flies never bite, so biting insects outdoors after a storm are real mosquitoes, and our mosquito control in Tucson service handles those.

How Do I Keep Drain Flies From Coming Back?

Keep every drain moving and clean. Drain flies come back when a drain sits unused or a film is allowed to rebuild, so prevention is mostly a habit, not a product. Here is the routine we suggest to Tucson homeowners after a problem is solved:

  • Run water for 30 seconds in every guest bath, casita and laundry drain once a week.
  • Brush the kitchen sink overflow slot and strainer every month.
  • Add a cup of water to garage and floor drains so the trap never dries out in summer heat.
  • Clean the shower and tub drain strainers of hair every few weeks.
  • Before a long trip or a snowbird season, flush every drain, then check them again when you return.

None of these steps costs anything but a few minutes, and they stop the film that drain flies need. A home that is traveled in and out of often, like a rental or a winter place, benefits the most.

Our Tucson branch serves the whole metro, including Oro Valley, Marana, Vail, Catalina Foothills, Green Valley, Sahuarita and Valencia West. If you are in Sahuarita, our Sahuarita and Quail Creek guide covers the outdoor side of flying pests.

You can see everything we do in town on our Tucson page, or request service online and we will get back to you. Bucksworth Home Services has been locally owned since 2013 by Jordan and Taylor Moore, and you can see how we work on our YouTube channel.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do you get rid of drain flies fast?

Scrub the inside of the drain with a stiff brush, treat it with an enzyme drain cleaner overnight and repeat for a week. Adults die off within days once the breeding film is gone.

Where do drain flies come from?

They breed in the slime layer inside drains, traps and overflow slots, and sometimes in other damp organic buildup. They are not "from nowhere"; a lightly used or dirty drain is almost always the source.

Do drain flies mean I have a sewer problem?

Not necessarily. Most of the time it is just film in one drain. If the flies come from many drains at once or you smell sewer gas, have a licensed plumber check your line, since that is outside what we do.

Are drain flies harmful?

They do not bite or sting, but they live in unsanitary film and can leave bacteria on surfaces they land on, so they are worth clearing quickly.

How long do drain flies take to go away?

Plan on seven to fourteen days after you start cleaning. Adults live about two weeks, and new ones stop appearing once the film is gone.

When should I call a pest control company?

Call if the flies persist after two weeks of cleaning, appear in several rooms or you cannot find the source. Tucson homeowners can reach us at (520) 284-9930.
